test_results_detail.console_errors: No errors related to new components (RadarChart, CompareMode, DatePicker, RadarPanel, ComparePoster). Only pre-existing noise: Recharts width=-1 warnings (asked to ignore), 404s for unrelated resources, 500 from a Stripe analytics call, WebGL GPU stall warning.

critical_code_review_comments: TrajectoryPage.jsx is now ~845 lines — recommend extracting CompareMode + its sub-components (DatePicker, RadarPanel, ComparePoster) into /app/frontend/src/components/trajectory/ for the next iteration (file-size guideline >700 lines).

Minor: DatePicker option label uses 🔒 emoji prefix for locked indices in the native select. This is fine functionally but inconsistent with the design system; the visible UI relies on the locked-click handler to gate, so the emoji is purely decorative inside the native dropdown.

Defensive: applyPreset('biggest') gates by isPremium AND biggestJump, but the click handler routes locked clicks through onLockedClick BEFORE calling applyPreset — so the isPremium check inside applyPreset is redundant but harmless. Not a bug.

context_for_next_testing_agent: Compare Mode is at /app/frontend/src/pages/TrajectoryPage.jsx line ~480 onwards. Test by intercepting trajectory + pass status endpoints BEFORE page.goto — gating logic is purely client-side. When asserting Stripe modal opened, look for 'embedded-checkout-inner' substring in frame URLs (the file has a hash suffix in production, e.g. 'embedded-checkout-inner-{40-char-hash}.html'). The Biggest-jump preset selects the consecutive pair with the largest positive overall delta (not first↔last). Default pair is first↔latest with scrub=1.
